text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I ran a prefix-cache TTL vs shard_count sim on the staging cluster this morning.

maria: Method: replayed 24h request trace with current allocator, measured per-GPU resident mem, fragmentation estimate, and prompt cache hit-rate.

maria: TL;DR: lowering TTL from 6h -> 30m reduced cache footprint but increased allocator fragmentation and workspace OOMs on long-seq tails.

alex: Can you drop the key numbers? % hit-rate and mem?

maria: Sure. With TTL=6h, shards=64: cache mem ~28GB, hit-rate 84%, 99p latency 210ms, fragmentation est 9%.

maria: With TTL=30m, shards=64: cache mem ~12GB, hit-rate 55%, 99p latency 270ms, fragmentation est 21%, saw 3 OOMs in 24h replay.

jonathan: Wait — fragmentation increased when cache shrank? that smells like allocator freelist churn + small alloc patterns

maria: Exactly. Short TTL causes many short-lived prefix entries, so we do more small frees/allocs and the workspace pool ends up with many small holes.

karen: Do we have breakdown by allocation size? maybe the workspace allocator bucketing isn't matching the live sizes.

maria: I produced a heatmap: most churn in 4–64KB allocations (kv blobs + small temp tensors). Our current pool chunk is 128KB, which leaves internal gaps.

maria: Profiling snippet:
```
# replay command
./sim_replay --trace=prod_24h.gz --ttl=30m --shards=64 --alloc=default --out=sim_ttl30m.json
```

alex: Two quick ideas: 1) decrease chunk size to 64KB for the small-bucket cache path; 2) reuse temp buffers across steps for the same request (reuse_policy=per-request).

jonathan: Reuse is promising but risky with KV cache concurrency. Need to ensure we don't hold onto buffers across coroutine hops.

maria: I prototyped buffer reuse in the runtime: per-request arena that resets at EOS. Early results: fragmentation dropped from 21% -> 11% and no OOMs in the sim.

maria: But it increased avg CPU for the allocator path by ~3% due to extra bookkeeping.

karen: Good tradeoff. Can we combine with shard resizing? fewer shards -> bigger per-shard prefix store -> fewer small allocations but higher eviction amplification.

maria: Simulation matrix I ran:
- TTL: [6h, 2h, 30m]
- shards: [32, 64, 128]
- allocator_chunk: [128k, 64k]

maria: Best result was TTL=2h, shards=32, allocator_chunk=64k + per-request reuse. Cache mem ~18GB, hit-rate 73%, fragmentation 8%, 99p latency 225ms, no OOMs.

jonathan: Nice. That seems like a practical sweet spot: small enough cache to save cost but not so small that allocator churn kills us.

alex: Can we make this dynamic? e.g., auto-tune shard_count and chunk size based on observed small-allocation churn signal.

maria: Proposed metric: small_alloc_rate (allocs <64KB per second) and fragmentation_est. If small_alloc_rate > threshold, flip allocator_chunk to 64k and enable per-request reuse.

karen: For rollout, suggest canary on dedicated pool with 10% traffic, collect 7-day signal (OOMs, 99p latency, alloc CPU).

perf-bot: deploy-checklist: add e2e sim with mixed seq lengths, update perf dashboard with small_alloc_rate, add kill-switch flag runtime.enable_reuse=false

alex: Who wants action items?

maria: I'll open an RFC with the sim artifacts + code patch for per-request arena. I'll also add the auto-tune PR sketch.

jonathan: I'll prototype the allocator_chunk dynamic toggler and a metric exporter for small_alloc_rate.

karen: I'll own the rollout plan and dashboards.

maria: Thanks. If we can get the canary in 2 weeks we can evaluate before next release. :thumbsup:

alex: Looks solid. One more ask — add a synthetic test with many concurrent short-prefix writes to stress the freelist.

maria: Good call, adding it to sim harness.

jonathan: I'll sync with infra to reserve a canary GPU pool.

perf-bot: noted. created ticket RW-8842 and linked sim artifacts.

maria: Closing loop — I'll post the sim jsons and the heatmap in this thread when uploaded.

alex: Thanks team.
